chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the believer supplicates to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding his need, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Delay its answer, out of desire for his voice and his supplication.' So when it is the Day of Judgment, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'My servant, you supplicated to Me, so I delayed your answer, and your reward is such and such; and you supplicated to Me regarding such and such, so I delayed answering you, and your reward is such and such.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'So the believer wishes that no supplication of his had been answered in the world, due to what he sees of the excellence of the reward.'
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah delay answering a believer's supplication?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the concept of 'Ikhtiyar' (divine choice) in supplication, where delay is not neglect but a means of accumulating greater reward. The Imam highlights that the believer's longing for Allah's response transforms the waiting period into an act of worship, resulting in such immense eschatological reward that the believer may prefer the delayed, high-value reward over immediate worldly fulfillment. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that patience in dua is a spiritual investment with exponential returns in the Hereafter.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Momin supplicates to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic regarding his need, so Allahazwj Mighty and Majetic is Saying: “Delay its Answer”, out of Desire to his voice and his supplication. So when it will be the Day of Judgment, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Say: “Myazwj servant! You supplicated to Meazwj but Iazwj Delayed its Answer, and your Rewards are such and such, and you supplication to Meazwj regarding such and such, but Iazwj Delayed Answering you and your Rewards are such and such”.
Heasws said: ‘So the Momin would wish that no supplication of his had been Answered in the world due to what he sees from the excellent Rewards’.
en.sarwar: 9. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Su’Dan ibn Muslim from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“A believing person may pray to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, for help and Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will say, ‘Hold back the answer to his prayer for the desire in his voice and prayer.’ When it will be the Day of Judgment Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will say, ‘My servant, you prayed to Me and I delayed your answer. So and so is your reward. You prayed to Me in such and such matters and I delayed your answer. Your reward is so and so.’
The Imam said, ‘The believing person then wishes that none of his prayers had been accepted in the worldly life. He will say so on finding such handsome rewards.’”
